name: Legislative
scope: U.S. Congress. Legislative-branch acts only: hearings, caucuses, sworn testimony, bills, amendments, enacted statutes, oversight demands.
excludes: Executive-branch implementation (Government). When a law creates an office or duty, the vote/enactment is credited here; the executive executing it is Government.
method: First-principles ladder ordered by increasing bindingness and political cost. Non-ontological. One-text-one-event: a single bill is counted once, at its highest stage reached.
read: Congress wrote the powers and never used them. Recognition, hearings, oversight architecture and a funding lever are all enacted — yet no subpoena, no enforcement body. Authority on paper, restraint in practice.
summary: Congress has written binding reporting duties, a protected channel, a public-records regime and funding leverage — but has never actually used its hard powers, and never enacted an independent enforcer. Power written everywhere, power used nowhere.
sourcingQuality: Strong — primary sources with URLs (govinfo, congress.gov, senate.gov, oversight.house.gov).

rungs.title: Organized legislative recognition
rungs.oneLiner: A committee/caucus formally owns the issue. e.g. UAP Caucus 2023 + SSCI Report 116-233.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Part of the legislature institutionally owns the issue and creates an official record. Non-binding, but a real political cost.
rungs.statusRationale: A caucus and a formal committee directive both exist on the record.

sources.label: SSCI Report 116-233 accompanying the IAA FY2021

rungs.title: Formal sworn hearings
rungs.oneLiner: On-record testimony under oath. e.g. House Oversight hearing, 26 July 2023.
rungs.firstPrinciples: The legislature stops requesting and starts testing evidence; sworn testimony exposes witnesses to perjury liability.
rungs.statusRationale: Multiple on-record hearings with sworn testimony have occurred. Discrete threshold, crossed.

sources.label: House Oversight hearing on UAP, 26 July 2023 (Graves, Fravor, Grusch)

rungs.title: Enacted oversight architecture
rungs.oneLiner: Statute imposes binding reporting duties. e.g. PL 117-81, PL 117-263.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A statute imposes recurring reporting/briefing duties with legal effect until amended or repealed.
rungs.statusRationale: Enacted law mandates a UAP office and annual reporting to Congress. Credit is the enactment of the duties, not the executive office's performance.
rungs.limitation: Some reporting duties carry termination dates and can be amended, repealed, or allowed to sunset.

rungs.title: Protected disclosure channel
rungs.oneLiner: Enacted (50 U.S.C. 3373b). Partial: no public route, no civil action.
rungs.firstPrinciples: This rung changes the legal position of people holding restricted information — overriding NDAs, protecting from reprisal.
rungs.statusRationale: Enacted and real, but amputated: no protected route to the public, no private civil action, transactional immunity absent. The Enhanced UAP Whistleblower Protection Act (proposed 2025) is not enacted.

rungs.title: Public-records disclosure regime
rungs.oneLiner: NARA collection + 25-yr rule. Partial: independent board stripped.
rungs.firstPrinciples: The statute creates public-facing disclosure duties and limits indefinite unexplained withholding.
rungs.statusRationale: Enacted (NARA collection, preservation, 25-year presumption), but the independent Review Board contemplated in the Senate proposal was stripped, and executive-originating bodies control the initial postponement decision.

rungs.title: Fiscal conditionality
rungs.oneLiner: Funding conditioned on disclosure (PL 118-31). Waived-SAP structures limit visibility.
rungs.firstPrinciples: The power of the purse is the hardest legislative leverage. Conditioning funds on disclosure adds a real consequence to concealment.
rungs.statusRationale: Enacted funding condition: appropriated funds may not support UAP activity in undisclosed special/restricted-access programs unless detailed to the appropriate committees. Achieved because the lever exists in statute; its non-use is captured separately at rung 7.
rungs.limitation: Scope bounded to that Act's funds. Waived/unacknowledged SAP architectures are designed to limit the budgetary visibility the condition depends on — a legal-structure limit, not a claim that any specific hidden program exists.

rungs.title: Compulsory power actually used
rungs.oneLiner: No UAP subpoena, contempt, or applied funding cutoff. Only a March 2026 request letter.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A paper power can stay politically costless. Invoking it (subpoena, contempt, applied funding cutoff) creates real conflict. Distinct from — and higher than — possessing the power.
rungs.statusRationale: No public record of a UAP-specific subpoena, contempt proceeding, or applied funding cutoff. The closest escalation is the House Oversight Task Force request letter of 31 March 2026 — a request, not compulsion.

sources.label: No qualifying source (near-miss: 31 March 2026 request letter)

rungs.title: Independent enforcement body
rungs.oneLiner: Schumer-Rounds, UAPDA, Burlison FY2027 passed a chamber. Partial: none enacted.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Replaces ad hoc committee confrontation with a standing, independent mechanism able to compel evidence and obtain judicial enforcement.
rungs.statusRationale: Repeatedly designed, never enacted. Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act (2023, board stripped in conference); UAP Disclosure Act of 2025 (tabled); Burlison amendment to NDAA FY2027 (House-passed 2026, has subpoena, lacks direct override, not enacted).

crossTrackNotes: This track counts the vote/enactment. The executive implementing any of these (operating AARO, constituting a board) is credited on Government, never here.
